notes: WP3, multi-GPU without disproportionate overhead: the three ways llama.cpp lays one model
over several GCDs, --split-mode layer (the default, every split measured until now), row
and tensor (experimental tensor parallelism), on 2, 4 and 8 GCDs, against the same model
on one GCD (c01 dense-one-gcd, moe-one-gcd) and as replicas (c01 scale-replicas).
Layer split adds memory, not speed: four GCDs as layers wrote no faster than one
(12-09-2026, c01 scale-split, c02 split4 against split8). Row and tensor cut each weight
across the GCDs and are what could make one request faster; batch 1 is the point of the
campaign, batch 16 says what they cost or give with many requests.
Needs the engine of 15-10-2026 (next12): --split-mode. An architecture tensor parallelism
does not cover fails its load and says so; that is a measurement, not a failure to retry.
Exclusive: the split's GCDs talk to each other over the node's links, which a neighbour
on the same links would share.
